title: Principal Investigator, Correlation Regime Lab
verdict_why: The case is not made in either direction: history still short (91/100); scoreboard still warming up (n=83/200); decisive reads 0.0% — below the 40% bar. I keep the watch open and keep gathering evidence.
verdict_plain: Cherry's verdict: hold and keep watching. The coupling evidence so far is neither strong enough to apply nor weak enough to withdraw — the watch stays open.
model_gates: APPLY_CANDIDATE nominates only. Adoption requires the runner's champion/challenger gates: held-out Brier improvement ≥ 2e-4, positive in both halves, family-wise α=0.05 with Bonferroni correction, ≥24h between adoptions. WITHDRAW recommends corrWeight 0. This file never changes a weight directly.

hypotheses.claim: When XRP and BTC are coupled (high rolling correlation), BTC’s recent drift tilts subsequent XRP moves in the same direction.
hypotheses.prediction: decisive coupling regimes align with 24h direction more often than chance

hypotheses.claim: The correlation-regime member beats the baseline forecast out-of-sample on Brier score.
hypotheses.prediction: member Brier < baseline Brier over n ≥ 200 scored forecasts

hypotheses.claim: Correlation regimes shift: coupling breaks down on idiosyncratic XRP news and rebuilds on macro moves.
hypotheses.prediction: decoupling episodes coincide with elevated XRP-specific volatility
hypotheses.test: regime transitions vs volatility from lab notes

hypotheses.claim: The coupling regime expresses itself often enough to matter — not a once-a-quarter curiosity.
hypotheses.prediction: decisive_frac ≥ 0.40 over rolling history once n ≥ 100

disciplines_applied.assessment: corr24h over the last day of aligned bars averages 0.867; coupled 96.7% of cycles. Correlation is an estimate with error bars, not a fact — the full day of shared history is what keeps it honest.
No edge to explain — and I will not pretend a decoupled drift was ever a signal.

The correlation is Pearson on log returns of time-aligned bars — change the alignment and the number changes, so alignment is part of the result. Error propagates: a bias built from two measurements is not twice as certain as one.
When in doubt I vote HOLD: adopting noise corrupts every forecast it touches, and that is the costliest error I can make.
Pipeline healthy: both bar series readable 96.7% of cycles; timestamps aligned exactly, gaps dropped not interpolated; same bars reproduce the same numbers.

Correlations regime-shift — altcoins decouple on idiosyncratic news and re-couple on macro moves. Everyone watching the same correlation watches it get arbitraged; the edge, if any, is in the conditionality, not in "BTC up means XRP up." That is why no APPLY verdict of mine ever skips out-of-sample proof.
Known: coupled 96.7% of cycles, decisive 0.0%. Unknown: whether the regime structure survives the next market break. Confidence: low — the honest answer.
Hypothesis ledger updated — statuses changed only where the evidence moved them; nothing was buried and nothing was accepted without a test.
I sign this verdict: HOLD. It is defensible from the record below, and I will reverse it the moment the evidence does.
